heading: Chap. xviii.—The body of Polycarp is burned.
paragraphs:
The centurion then, seeing the strife excited by the Jews,
placed the body[444] in the midst of the fire, and consumed it.
Accordingly, we afterwards took up his bones, as being more
94precious than the most exquisite jewels, and more purified[445]
than gold, and deposited them in a fitting place, whither,
being gathered together, as opportunity is allowed us, with
joy and rejoicing, the Lord shall grant us to celebrate the
anniversary[446] of his martyrdom, both in memory of those
who have already finished their course,[447] and for the exercising
and preparation of those yet to walk in their steps.
